video_title: Nets Fest Convos: Coach Fernández, Julius Randle, Day'Ron Sharpe, Moe Wagner and Keon Ellis

quotes.speaker: Julius Randle
quotes.summary_phrase: Julius Randle on the Nets' mix of experience and youth
quotes.excerpt: we have a good mix of experience with youth and I think that's going to take us

text_blocks.speaker: Jordi Fernández
text_blocks.text: How do you feel about the squad and how we're looking forward?

text_blocks.speaker: Julius Randle
text_blocks.text: It feels great for many reasons. Acquiring a three-time All-Star is extremely helpful, but it sets the tone for the rest of the young guys. Bringing guys that have been there before, Julius, Michael, Kian, Mo, Terence, so we have a good mix of experience with youth and I think that's going to take us to take the next step.

quotes.speaker: Julius Randle
quotes.summary_phrase: Julius Randle on his leadership style and learning from Kobe Bryant
quotes.excerpt: I just try to lead by example. I had the greatest example in a veteran and mentor in Kobe

text_blocks.speaker: Jordi Fernández
text_blocks.text: What is it that you're teaching the young guys as they're coming up? And at the same time, what are you being taught by those in front of you?

text_blocks.speaker: Julius Randle
text_blocks.text: I just try to lead by example. I had the greatest example in a veteran and mentor in Kobe growing up. I realize the impact. I look at Yae, I look at Michael, Joshua, Noah, all those young guys, Drake, and I remember being in their shoes and I understand the impact that being had on me as a young player and it kind of set me up for my career of how I approach every single day, how I approach a practice, how I approach a game, how I approach a workout.

quotes.speaker: Day'Ron Sharpe
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenyon Martin on Day'Ron Sharpe's offensive rebounding and court intelligence
quotes.excerpt: The offensive rebounding thing is motor for one, but it's intelligence and knowing the flight of the ball

text_blocks.speaker: Jordi Fernández
text_blocks.text: Kenyon, knowing what you know about Day'Ron's game, what part of his game do you wish you had when you played?

text_blocks.speaker: Kenyon Martin
text_blocks.text: The offensive rebounding thing is motor for one, but it's intelligence and knowing the flight of the ball and different things of that nature. You can't teach that, you can't coach that. We did a drill when I was in college called get opposite where it was offensive rebounding drill and we drilled it. It's not a natural thing for everyone to have, especially bigs, the flight of the ball and determine where it's going to land.

quotes.speaker: Kenyon Martin
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenyon Martin on the importance of relentless pressure in the paint
quotes.excerpt: Don't nobody want to have to deal with that possession after possession, quarter after quarter, game after game

text_blocks.speaker: Jordi Fernández
text_blocks.text: What do you see in Day'Ron's game that you wish you had?

text_blocks.speaker: Kenyon Martin
text_blocks.text: Don't nobody want to have to deal with that possession after possession, quarter after quarter, game after game. It's what we talked about earlier, right? Being relentless, each possession matters. Don't nobody want to deal with that possession after possession. You don't want to have to box him out. You can't. It's exhausting, and they're not going to do it. It's only going to get better the more experience he has, the more minutes he plays, the more meaningful games he plays.

quotes.speaker: Kenyon Martin
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenyon Martin on the importance of self-critique for NBA players
quotes.excerpt: If you're not having self-critique and self-conversation on how to be better at whatever it is you're doing

text_blocks.speaker: Jordi Fernández
text_blocks.text: What has been your foundation in your career?

text_blocks.speaker: Kenyon Martin
text_blocks.text: It's this thing that most of us have in our house. It's right by your sink. It's like a reflection thing. It's called a mirror. You look at yourself every day, which you should. And if you're not having self-critique and self-conversation on how to be better at whatever it is you're doing, it's just that we play sports for a living. Muggsy Bogues was 5'3", Michael Adams was 5'7", Earl Boykins was 5'5". There's guys that's done it. It's a little harder now because of the way the game has transitioned, but somebody probably told them the same thing: are you too small? It don't matter. Long as you go out and compete and you're going to fight, you're going to get some looks.

quotes.speaker: Keon Ellis
quotes.summary_phrase: Keon Ellis on the process of finding his role as a young player
quotes.excerpt: the biggest question was not the skill and whether you can do it, it's more about realizing what type of player you want to be

text_blocks.speaker: Jordi Fernández
text_blocks.text: What is your perspective on the young guys that we have on the squad so far and how you feel like your leadership could impact them moving forward?

text_blocks.speaker: Keon Ellis
text_blocks.text: At the end of the day, I think it's not easy for young guys, especially if there's a lot of them, because the competition level is super high. And I think for me as a young player going through that process, the biggest question was not the skill and whether you can do it, it's more about realizing what type of player you want to be and how are you the most effective and how are you going to help a franchise win. So finding that out takes some time and takes some honest conversation.

quotes.speaker: Moe Wagner
quotes.summary_phrase: Moe Wagner on the simplicity of basketball and the importance of doing your job
quotes.excerpt: basketball is a simple game and I think the way that I approach every game, practice, every day

text_blocks.speaker: Jordi Fernández
text_blocks.text: What's it like to make the transition to a new team, but knowing that there's expectations on you already?

text_blocks.speaker: Moe Wagner
text_blocks.text: I don't think there's no pressure. I mean, basketball is a simple game and I think the way that I approach every game, practice, every day is it just makes it that much easier because I mean to me it's just go out there and do your job and I mean if you go out there and do your job everything will take care of itself.

quotes.speaker: Moe Wagner
quotes.summary_phrase: Moe Wagner on the importance of being a hard-working, diverse team
quotes.excerpt: I've always known that Brooklyn is something of a hard-working environment that everybody prides themselves on

text_blocks.speaker: Jordi Fernández
text_blocks.text: What did you know about Brooklyn before you signed here and what have you learned new now that you're here?

text_blocks.speaker: Moe Wagner
text_blocks.text: I mean, I will say that I've always known that Brooklyn is something of a hard-working environment that everybody prides themselves on, that's also very, very diverse. And yeah, those those things kind of, yeah, nothing changed after I signed here, just that I now go to work here. It's pretty awesome and I've really enjoyed that. My favorite player growing up was Kevin Garnett and to kind of I always think when I like shoot in the morning, I'm like, Kevin Garnett used to warm up here too, you know.
